blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: In this paper, we propose a Unified Law for Visual Tasks, which could be further divided into Four Laws of Computer Vision, with the goal of enabling a single framework or method to uniformly train on and perform nearly all visual tasks. Our starting point is an inspiration and hypothesis: if the world information is encoded into image, which we call World Snapshots, then image processing is world processing, and image generation is World Snapshot generation. Furthermore, if all visual and visualization tasks can be reformulated as generation tasks, then a unified method, World Snapshot Models (WSMs), can perform the vast majority of visual tasks, much as large language models have largely unified natural language processing. This paper validates these laws across more than 1,000 trained and evaluated visual tasks (defined by distinct input-output mappings) and presents a unified training framework for future visual-task research and applications.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们提出了"视觉任务统一法"(United Law for Visual Interviews),可以进一步划分为"计算机视觉四法"(Four Laws of Computer Vision),其目标是使单一的框架或方法能够统一培训和完成几乎所有的视觉任务. 我们的出发点是一个启发和假设:如果世界信息被编码成图像,我们称之为"世界快照",那么图像处理就是世界处理,而图像生成就是"世界快照"一代. 此外,如果所有可视化和可视化任务都可以重新制定为生成任务,那么一种统一的方法——世界快照模型(World Snapshot Models)(WSMs)可以完成绝大多数的可视化任务,就像大型语言模型已经基本统一了自然语言处理一样. 本文验证了1,000多项经过培训和评价的视觉任务(由不同的输入-输出绘图界定)的这些法律,并为未来的视觉任务研究和应用提供了一个统一的培训框架。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Recently, many researchers now expect computer vision to develop a unified model as powerful as large language models [ 1 , 2 ] , often referring to such a model as a world model [ 3 , 4 ] .
This expectation is usually motivated by the hope that ideas such as “predicting the next token” or “predicting the next state” can be transferred to the visual domain [ 5 , 6 , 7 ] .
However, this view faces two fundamental difficulties: visual data cannot be fully summarized by a simple prompt-answer format, and computer vision tasks appear in many different forms.
In this paper, we therefore attempt to formulate an ideal World Model that can move beyond these limitations and improve the unity and generality of visual methods.
blocks.zh:
最近,许多研究者现在期望计算机视觉能开发出一个像大语言模型一样强大的统一模型[1,2],常指这样的模型如世界模型[3,4].
这种期望的动机通常是希望“预测下个信号”或“预测下个状态”之类的想法能够被转移到视觉领域[5、6、7]。
然而,这种观点面临两个基本困难:视觉数据不能用简单的即时回答格式来完全总结,计算机视觉任务以许多不同的形式出现.
因此,在本文中,我们试图制定一个理想的世界模式,能够超越这些限制,提高视觉方法的统一性和通俗性.

blocks.en:
Insight and Hypothesis. First, we argue that what the visual domain truly needs is to encode all information into the image itself.
More specifically, if all information can be encoded into the image itself, then two-dimensional image generation becomes lossless world generation. 1 1 1 This statement is the Unified Law proposed in this paper. Physicists at the end of the last century referred to a similar idea as the holographic principle and provided systematic arguments showing that [ 8 , 9 , 10 ] , under special conditions, an ( n + 1 ) (n+1) -dimensional space can be encoded into an n n -dimensional space. This also supports our view that an information-rich image can approximate a world frame.

更具体地说,如果所有信息都可以被编码入图像本身,那么二维图像生成就会成为无所失落的世界代. 1个 1,本说明为本文提出的"统一法". 上个世纪末的物理学家将类似的想法称为"全息学原理",并提供了系统的论点,表明[8,9,10],在特殊条件下,一个(n+ 1)(n+1)-维空间可以被编码为n-维空间. 这也支持我们的观点,即信息丰富的图像可以接近世界框架。

blocks.en:
To verify the existence of this Unified Law, we introduce an image data format with up to 256 channels named World Snapshot Graphics (.wsg).
This format stores additional information, including spatial structure, pose, physics, audio, and semantics, in extra channels.
We then attempt to train a model to generate images in this format, using the generation process itself as a test of the proposed law.

为了验证这个"统一法"的存在,我们引入了一种图像数据格式,其中多达256个频道被命名为"世界快照图形"(.wsg).
这种格式将额外的信息,包括空间结构,姿势,物理,音频,和语义,存储在额外的通道中.
然后,我们试图培训一种模型,以这种格式生成图像,利用生成过程本身来测试拟议的法律。

Derived Implications and Research Reframing. Furthermore, a task is a visual task as long as either its input or its output is visual information. Then, visual tasks can be abstracted at a macro level into generation, estimation, conditional control, and reconstruction. 2 2 2 These correspond to the four sub-laws. In our experiments, we find that preparing four types of interfaces can support almost all visual tasks. These four broad categories are not arbitrary: they correspond to the four fundamental directional relations formed when RGB, text, and non-RGB world attributes serve as conditions or targets. Prior work covers each category in a narrow form, such as generating only RGB or estimating a few attributes from RGB; we call this narrow vision, and its extension to every world attribute broad vision. More directly, we do not want to train four separate classes of world-processing models for generation, estimation, conditional control, and reconstruction; we treat them all as forms of generation.
Figure presents these four task families as Lex
I–IV. Together, they refine and extend the Unified Law by treating all four as forms of generation, thereby avoiding having to train four broad classes of world snapshot/frame processing models.

blocks.en:
The Elephant in the Room. For a concrete method, we should consider how to train a unified visual generation model whose backbone can be reused by countless conditions to perform one or multiple rounds of inference.
However, this immediately raises a long-standing challenge: training efficiency.
We should not substantially increase the number of parameters merely to make one model master more than 1,000 visual tasks; instead, we should aim for a regime in which the model’s capabilities expand by orders of magnitude while its parameter count grows only slightly.
ControlNet [ 11 ] , LoRA [ 12 ] , MoE [ 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 ] , IP-Adapter [ 17 ] , and IC-Control Style [ 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 ] are five commonly used approaches for expanding the capabilities of existing models, but even LoRA, which can acquire a new capability within several hours to several days, becomes insufficient when facing thousands of tasks.

然而,这立即提出了长期的挑战:培训效率。
我们不应该仅仅为了让一个模型的主人公超过1000个视觉任务而大量增加参数的数量;相反,我们应当力求建立一种制度,使模型的能力按数量级增长,而其参数数却略有增长。

Its core idea is to assign each modality to a separate learning stream connected

blocks.en: Contributions. The main contributions of this paper are summarized as follows: • We propose Unified Law for Visual Tasks , which organizes all visual tasks into four broad categories—generation, estimation, conditional control, and reconstruction—and reformulates all four under a common generative perspective, providing a theoretical path toward unifying large-scale visual tasks. • To support large-scale, complex visual reasoning through arbitrary, cyclic, and chained transformations among many modalities, we introduce World Snapshot Graphics (.wsg) , a conceptual world-frame representation and flexible image format. Its world-frame abstraction provides a macro-level logic for understanding and managing modalities, while up to 256 channel IDs provide a flexible operational address space for spatial, pose, physical, audio, semantic, and other world information. • We introduce World Snapshot Models (WSMs) , a unified framework connecting the Four Laws to four generative interfaces through a many-to-many correspondence. The Laws provide a macro-level conceptual organization of visual tasks; the interfaces are the minimal operational basis determined by the properties of task conditions and targets and provide concrete training schemes. • We propose TunnelingNet , an efficient capability-expansion method that independently trains and registers lightweight task networks inside a shared frozen visual generator, enabling rapid scaling to thousands of tasks. Each generated world state can directly condition the next TunnelingNet, forming a self-contained visual-processing loop across all four broad task categories and revealing an initial visual chain of thought in a purely visual model. This composition opens a path to large-scale, complex visual reasoning: the task space expands as modalities are added, while executable visual chains grow exponentially with chain depth.

Multimodal Joint Generation . Our method builds on the generative formulation discussed above,
since RF/FM-based DiTs have recently become a common backbone for more powerful visual generation systems:
Open-source image and video generation models such as Flux [ 26 , 31 ] , Wan-Video [ 32 ] , and LTX [ 33 , 34 ] have first advanced the capability of visual generation.
More recently, models such as Google Veo [ 35 ] , OminiControl [ 36 , 37 ] , Vision Banana [ 38 ] , and UniVidX [ 39 ] have attempted large-scale multimodal joint generation.
These generative methods can be viewed as attempts to pursue a goal similar to ours; however, due to resource constraints,
their exploration is still not sufficiently thorough or deep. 4 4 4 According to timelines recorded by third-party systems,
we began exploring this direction two years earlier than related work, and our exploration is substantially deeper, allowing our public papers to cover roughly 50–150 times more tasks.

blocks.en: 3.1 World Snapshot Graphics

blocks.en:
We introduce World Snapshot Graphics ( .wsg ) as a unified image format for representing World Snapshots.
A .wsg sample is an image-like representation addressed by up to 256 channel IDs, where standard visual appearance occupies part of the representation and auxiliary channels encode richer world attributes. The 256 channels are a management convention: channel IDs form an address space currently capped at 256, and string names would serve equally well. Each task reads and generates only its own channels, never a full 256-channel tensor; all configured tasks currently use 115 channel IDs, so new types of world information can be added without changing the format.
We used datasets including AVIS [ 40 ] , Articulation-XL2.0 [ 41 ] , ShapeNetSem [ 42 ] , and MatSynth [ 43 ] , and processed this data using our developed WSG dependency library, extracting information from RGB estimation and then injecting the RGB and additional information into WSG files.

blocks.en: 3.2 Four Generative Interfaces of Training

blocks.en:
We organize WSG training as a directed graph centered at RGB. Text first enters
visual space through text → RGB \mathrm{text}\to\mathrm{RGB} . Around RGB, every WSG
modality is a node, and every directed edge is one visual task realized by a
TunnelingNet. Each TunnelingNet is a lightweight capability network distributed
through multiple layers inside the frozen generative backbone; training it
redirects the backbone’s generation trajectory toward one task without modifying
the shared model.
As shown in Figure 2 , the released dense WSM graph
configures 3,042 visual task mappings around one shared generative backbone.
The benchmark in this paper provides trained models and end-to-end inference results on the evaluation set for 1,148 dense TunnelingNets; accordingly,
1,148 is the task count reported for WSM in the main paper. Sparse digitized
tasks use their declared native metrics and are not included in this count.
Their detailed native evaluation will be provided in an expanded version.
Extending evaluation to the remaining dense mappings requires no change to the unified interfaces or
model architecture. 5 5 5 If ResNet enables models to be trained especially deep, even with thousands of layers, our TunnelingNet enables models to be trained on thousands of visual tasks.

Around an RGB-based generative backbone, the WSG graph represents visual tasks
as directed condition–target edges. A scalable WSM must add edges without
replicating the full generator. TunnelingNet
therefore factorizes learning into a shared World Snapshot generator and
lightweight capability networks distributed throughout the frozen backbone. Given the typed edge ℋ k \mathcal{H}_{k} and its role assignment ρ k \rho_{k} , TunnelingNet models the transformation as p θ , ϕ k ​ ( 𝐱 𝒯 k ∣ 𝐱 𝒞 k , 𝐩 ) , p_{\theta,\phi_{k}}\left(\mathbf{x}_{\mathcal{T}_{k}}\mid\mathbf{x}_{\mathcal{C}_{k}},\mathbf{p}\right), (3) where θ \theta is a frozen rectified-flow visual generator, ϕ k \phi_{k} contains the
trainable parameters of TunnelingNet k k , and 𝐩 \mathbf{p} is the text prompt or
modality prompt. The same backbone therefore supports many directed edges, and
the marginal parameter cost of a new edge is the cost of its tunnel. WSM is one
modular model comprising the shared backbone θ \theta , a resident task-indexed
set of TunnelingNets { ϕ k } \{\phi_{k}\} , and an explicit task router. TunnelingNets can be
optimized independently and physically sharded for parallel training and
distribution; these are training and storage choices, not model boundaries.
At inference, a task key activates one TunnelingNet, while a visual chain
activates a selected TunnelingNet sequence. This yields one WSM with many generative
paths.

We find that dense and sparse prediction need not form two independent task

suppression, or connected-component analysis recovers the original sparse
structure.

blocks.en: 4.1 Attention Topology

blocks.en:
In this ablation, NJA uses the same target-side low-rank parameterization as MTA
and serves as our LoRA native-attention baseline. MTA changes only the
attention routing; the trainable parameter count, data, optimizer, batch size,
and training schedule remain fixed.
Native Joint Attention performs one softmax over the pooled text, target,
condition, and reference keys. In a controlled TunnelingNet 270 comparison at 140
updates, NJA obtained a validation MSE of 0.1917, compared with 0.2155 for MTA,
an 11.0% reduction. We therefore retain NJA for narrow visual generation.
Figure 5 (a) pairs the directly recorded
validation curves with the condition, selected NJA output, and target at
update 100. This result reflects the different requirements for conditioning
information in RGB generation and other modality estimation tasks. Modality
Tunneling Attention aims to limit the influence of the input RGB on the target
generation path, allowing conditioning information to act on the target through
an independent one-way channel. This mechanism is suitable for estimation,
simple conditional control, and inverse-rendering tasks because it can preserve
the target modality’s own generation process and prevent the input evidence
from dominating. However, conditional RGB generation typically requires edges,
normals, or other conditions to make larger changes to the structure and
content of the reference RGB, and therefore requires fuller interaction among
the condition, text, reference image, and target sequences. Native Joint
Attention places these sequences in the same attention space, allowing every
token to influence the entire generation sequence and thereby enabling the
conditioning information to globally reorganize the RGB generation path.
Therefore, Native Joint Attention is better suited to conditional RGB
generation, whereas Modality Tunneling Attention is better suited to non-RGB
estimation and reconstruction tasks that require the scope of the input
influence to be controlled.

The other three interfaces have heterogeneous, often deterministic non-RGB
targets. Here, joint normalization forces target self-attention and condition

representation path and learns a separately normalized tunnel between different
modal descriptions of the same underlying visual content. Concretely, MTA
preserves the text–target self path and adds an independently normalized
target-to-condition path.

blocks.en: 4.2 Condition Routing and Tunnel Placement

blocks.en:
Routing is nontrivial because the pretrained backbone introduced in
Section 3 is an image-editing model. Its native interface accepts
a text prompt and an optional RGB reference—the image to be edited—and uses
the resulting preservation prior while generating the target. TunnelingNet
additionally exposes clean condition lanes for WSG modalities and RGB
observations. The same RGB evidence can therefore enter either as a native
editable reference or as a condition: the former encourages the backbone to
preserve the supplied image, whereas the latter treats it as evidence rather
than content to copy. A second choice is tunnel placement: we can adapt both
the condition and target lanes, or train only the target-side tunnel while
leaving all evidence lanes on the frozen backbone.

condition branch and disable the native reference slot, so the current
Normal remains the state-defining evidence. Accordingly, TunnelingNet 270 is the only selected configuration that uses the native
RGB-reference slot. TunnelingNets 003 and 313 route RGB as condition evidence, while
TunnelingNet 275 has no RGB input.

blocks.en:
Figure 7 (d) isolates tunnel placement under the
same 100-update budget. Both variants recover comparable major Edge structure,
and adapting the condition side adds no visible structural gain. This does not
mean that condition evidence is ignored: clean Normal and RGB 1 tokens still
enter the separately normalized MTA path. Rather, the result locates the
task-specific learning burden at the target readout, which must translate
already informative frozen evidence into the requested output modality. It is
the practical counterpart of the color-vision analogy in
Section 1 : modality-specific streams need not acquire a common
internal interpretation, or learn to “understand one another,” to describe
the same underlying state. The target tunnel learns only the translation needed
by its output. Removing condition-side reinterpretation therefore reduces the
optimization burden and keeps condition states adapter-independent, allowing
one condition forward pass to be shared by many TunnelingNets. We consequently
train only the target tunnel, the smallest effective design. The panel also
reveals the complementary role of visual
evidence: the Normal estimate alone omits fine structures smoothed away during
estimation, whereas providing RGB 1 as additional evidence enables the
inverse-rendering TunnelingNet to recover them. This cross-modal completion provides
an empirical basis for Chain of Visual (CoV) reasoning, in which evidence
retained in one visual state resolves information absent from another. With
routing and tunnel placement fixed, the
remaining objective-shaping choice is quantified in
Table 4 and analyzed next.

blocks.en: 4.3 Rectified-Flow Objective
blocks.zh: 4.3 经更正的目标

blocks.en:
The initial dense-task experiments exposed two failure modes. Normal
predictions retained the correct coarse shape but drifted toward low-saturation
mean colors; sparse Edge predictions were progressively overwhelmed by their
black background. We therefore tested task-agnostic objective changes rather
than modality-specific losses. Table 4 compares
plain rectified flow, single-step clean-latent prediction, high-noise anchoring,
and annealed multi-resolution noise. Every model is evaluated by the same
plain velocity MSE at t = 1 t=1 . High-noise anchoring, which assigns half of the
training samples to t = 0.999 t=0.999 , is best on both representative target types and
reduces their mean validation error by 42.6% relative to the baseline.
Figure 8 shows that this advantage is not
merely numerical. For RGB-to-Normal, plain rectified flow and multi-resolution
noise recover the coarse layout but weaken the chromatic separation that
encodes surface orientation; the anchored model retains a more saturated,
spatially coherent field. For Normal-to-Edge, the same alternatives lose much
of the sparse contour support to the dominant black background, whereas
anchoring preserves connected structure. Single-step prediction is competitive
in Table 4 , but its decoded outputs are less
consistent across these dense and sparse targets. High-noise anchoring is thus
the only tested objective that improves the shared validation metric while also
preserving the modality-specific information visible after decoding.

blocks.en:
We also ablated low-noise timestep shifting, Min-SNR weighting, and Huber loss.
Huber produced the cleanest early visual results, and Min-SNR better resisted
late degradation, but neither was a consistent default. In particular,
enabling all three gradually drove outputs toward the target mean: Normal kept
its shape but faded, while Edge disappeared into the black background. This
qualitative behavior is not captured reliably by a weighted training loss,
which is why we retain fixed plain-MSE validation and inspect the decoded output
throughout training. The final concise recipe is therefore high-noise
anchoring alone, with timestep shifting, Min-SNR, Huber, single-step prediction,
and multi-resolution noise disabled. With this recipe, the four representative
TunnelingNets reach stable solutions within a 500-update ablation budget, compared with
the 5,000-update budget used by the earlier native setup.

blocks.en:
Using a fixed evaluation example and inference seed within each row, the sequence
reveals a consistent coarse-to-structured transition. The first tens of updates
establish the target modality and broad spatial support; later updates sharpen
task-specific geometry, improve structural continuity, and suppress residual
artifacts. This trend appears across dense estimation, RGB synthesis, sparse
conditional control, and inverse rendering despite their different output
statistics. Most importantly, the update-200 predictions have been trained on
only 200 sampled examples. They are therefore evidence that the proposed
routing and objective acquire a new visual mapping at minute scale, rather than
requiring conventional long-horizon fine-tuning. These early outputs provide
acquisition evidence and are not treated as final convergence. Later-checkpoint
comparisons will be provided in an expanded version.

A model could produce a plausible depth map, normal map, or mask without

same predictions with targets belonging to other inputs. An output that only
repeats a generic modality pattern receives essentially the same error after
the shift. A prediction that follows its own input loses agreement.
Section 5.2 shows the latter: correct
pairing reduces error in every interface, by 41.4% over the whole task graph,
and the median TunnelingNet loses 51.9% of its agreement after targets are shifted.
The thousand-task result therefore reflects sample-specific visual relations.

blocks.en:
Table 8 covers five representative established design
paradigms: new trainable parameter blocks (ControlNet), the MoE-style
multi-expert adapter in UniControl, LoRA (DMP),
expert-based MoE-family architectures—the mixture-of-transformers in MODUS
and strict sparse-MoE diffusion in Scaling Diffusion Perception—and
IC-Wrapper methods (T2I-Adapter and Uni-ControlNet). WSM introduces internal
trajectory tunneling. The three blocks correspond to Interfaces A – C :
RGB-to-depth estimation, Edge-to-RGB generation, and any-to-any control.
We also include VGGT as a task-specific depth estimator.
Interface C evaluates transfers among edge, relative depth, surface
normal, and human-part segmentation signals. Both WSM and MODUS support a
broader transfer inventory; we select these tasks as a representative
cross-section of structured understanding, spanning object and region
boundaries, scene-scale spatial organization, local surface orientation, and
human semantics. Across all three externally comparable interfaces and all five representative
tasks, WSM leads every reported quality metric, demonstrating that its advantage
holds across all five adaptation paradigms. Interface D combines first-frame RGB evidence
with a later auxiliary observation, for which we found no released image-level
method with matching inputs. Most remaining mappings enabled by this interface
similarly define new task settings without a like-for-like external comparator.

web-scale pretraining corpora of large foundation models. We therefore use the
AVIS evaluation set, which is less commonly used for dense prediction, and generate
the task annotations evaluated here ourselves. This choice reduces the
likelihood of direct overlap with existing image–annotation pairs. None of the
evaluation images or annotations is used to train WSM. A semantic analysis of the
scene captions also finds almost no close match between the evaluation scenes and the
WSM training descriptions. Every method receives the same AVIS
inputs and targets. The external methods use their released checkpoints, and
WSM uses its trained TunnelingNets without further optimization. The WSM TunnelingNets for depth and Edge-to-RGB use
TunnelingNets 1 and 424; TunnelingNet 424 uses its recommended native-reference route.
Interface C uses TunnelingNets 275, 119, and 434 for Normal-to-Edge,

The comparison covers substantially different routes to visual adaptation:
DMP uses LoRA-based diffusion perception; ControlNet introduces a trainable
parameter block; IP-Adapter and T2I-Adapter add image- or condition-specific
adapters; UniControl uses a MoE-style adapter; MODUS is a large sparse MoE; and
VGGT uses discriminative feed-forward regression. WSM is not specialized to any
one of their output domains. The same frozen backbone and the same tunneling
principle outperform these alternatives across depth, conditional RGB, and
condition-to-condition surface prediction. The award-winning comparisons make
this breadth especially concrete: WSM exceeds the CVPR 2025 Best Paper Award recipient VGGT on all five displayed depth
measures, and it exceeds the ICCV 2023 Best Paper Award recipient ControlNet on all seven conditional-generation measures. It also
outperforms the reference-enabled IP-Adapter–ControlNet combination on those
seven measures. The result is therefore a cross-paradigm improvement,
not an isolated gain over one architecture family.

The three evaluations isolate complementary concerns. Section 5.4 compares representative methods on
a common held-out set; Section 5.5 removes possible image-level pretraining overlap; and this section replaces the
WSG annotation convention with public annotators. In this final setting, WSM
remains strongest in conditional RGB generation and every structured transfer,
while retaining the best depth-boundary precision.
Across the five tasks, it outperforms award-winning specialized systems, modern
diffusion perception models, reference-conditioned adapters, and a 14B MoE
model, while adapting only a 12.5M-parameter TunnelingNet for each task. The 23 first-place and three second-place results show that WSM’s
advantage persists across new visual content, independent target definitions,
three interfaces, five representative tasks, and fundamentally different
modeling paradigms. This directly demonstrates that TunnelingNet can make far
more effective and powerful use of a frozen generative backbone through
extremely lightweight training, thereby adding strong new capabilities at
scale. This represents an advance over the prior paradigm-level approaches
evaluated here.

In Section 3 , we introduced four generative interfaces as
practical training configurations. They should not be confused with the four
high-level task families derived from the Unified Law—generation, estimation,
conditional control, and reconstruction. The task families describe what a
visual system is asked to do, whereas the interfaces specify how conditions and
targets are connected during training. Our experiments show that these four
interface configurations are sufficient to instantiate almost all evaluated
visual tasks.

separately presents the final categorical outputs. The remaining specialized

WSM can admit named nodes outside the fixed 256-channel WSG schema,
provided that the new variable has an aligned, machine-readable representation.

blocks.en: 7 Discussion
blocks.zh: 7 讨论情况

blocks.en: 7.1 Experimental Evidence
blocks.zh: 7.1 实验证据

blocks.en:
Our ablation study shows how TunnelingNet acquires a new visual route. We find
that attention topology, evidence routing, tunnel placement, and high-noise
trajectory supervision all shape how quickly a task-specific TunnelingNet learns its target
representation while preserving the RGB prior. The resulting configuration
produces recognizable structure within tens of updates and reaches up to
approximately 100 × 100\times greater training efficiency than the
parameter-matched native-attention baseline. Our quantitative study then asks
how widely this recipe holds: it evaluates 1,148 visual tasks, with one
independently deployable TunnelingNet per task, across 39 output groups, four
interfaces, and 18,191 end-to-end inference evaluations. Our qualitative study lets us inspect the visual relationships behind
those numbers across geometry, articulated humans, motion, physical
properties, materials, PBR appearance, segmentation, categorical identity,
and RGB synthesis. Together, our experiments give a consistent picture: a
shared generator can learn a wide vocabulary of World Snapshot transformations
when each route receives focused parameters and clearly routed evidence.

blocks.en: 7.2 Unified Task Graph and Model Scale
blocks.zh: 7.2 统一任务图和模型规模

blocks.en:
Each WSM task is a directed path from available evidence to a World Snapshot
target. Moving a variable from the condition side to the target side asks the
model to generate that variable. RGB therefore becomes one node in a much
larger generative domain that also includes geometry, pose, motion, material,
physics, semantics, and audio. This construction makes training naturally
parallel: every edge shares the frozen backbone, while its small tunnel can be
scheduled, optimized, and validated independently. It also makes capabilities
compositional. A generated variable can become evidence for the next edge, so
longer visual chains can be assembled from learned paths.
blocks.zh:
每一次WSM任务都是从现有证据到"世界快照"的定向路径.
目标。 将变量从条件侧移到目标侧询问
生成变量的模型。 RGB因此成为一个多的节点
包括几何、姿势、运动、物质
物理,语义,和音频。 这样的训练是自然的
平行:每个边缘共享被冻结的骨干,而其小隧道可以是
计划,优化,独立验证. 也能创造能力
组成。 生成的变量可以成为下一个边缘的证据,所以
更长的视觉链可以从所学的路径组装.

blocks.en:
The complete modular WSM comprises one shared backbone, a resident
collection of trained TunnelingNets and an explicit task router. Independent TunnelingNet
optimization and physical sharding of the TunnelingNet files enable parallel training and modular
distribution without changing this model boundary. All TunnelingNets remain
registered together, while a task key sparsely activates one edge and a visual
chain activates a selected sequence. This resident-versus-active organization
is analogous to sparsely activated expert models. WSM routes with an explicit
visual-task key; conventional expert models commonly learn their gating. We verified that each of the 1,148 frozen dense TunnelingNets
contains exactly 12,510,208 tunnel parameters, giving 14.362B TunnelingNet parameters
in total. Together with the 3.9B visual backbone and 0.282B parameters from the
180 deployed categorical refiners, the complete resident visual parameter bank

blocks.en:
Most computer-vision models are built around one task, and broadly capable
systems usually collect a small set of task-specific interfaces. WSM v1 places 1,148 evaluated tasks inside one generative system, while
its released dense task graph configures 3,042 possible mappings. Relative to the conventional scope of one to ten tasks, this expands
the task count by roughly two to three orders of magnitude. It also changes the
unit of progress: we can grow one directed generative graph by adding World
Snapshot variables and routes, and every new route becomes part of the same
model.

blocks.en:
The central result therefore reaches beyond any individual benchmark score. A
scientific law is useful when it compresses many apparently separate phenomena
into one practical rule. Our experiments provide large-scale evidence for
such a compression in computer vision: geometry, pose, motion, material,
physics, semantics, audio, and appearance become World Snapshots, and
generation becomes their common computational operation. TunnelingNet makes
this principle trainable in parallel, the directed graph makes it compositional,
and the shared backbone makes thousands of routes deployable as one WSM. This
is the law-scale ambition of the Unified Law for Visual Tasks: to organize a
growing field of visual capabilities through one reusable generative
principle. WSM v1 Augustus is its first large-scale realization, and the 3,042 mappings in its dense task graph provide an immediate path for expansion.

blocks.en: 7.4 Unifying and Expanding Computer Vision

blocks.en:
This section tests the central scope claim of the Unified Law. We ask two
questions. First, can the established tasks of computer vision be expressed
within the WSM interface system? Second, after those established tasks are
removed, how many tasks evaluated by WSM define genuinely new visual
problems? The first question measures unification ; the second measures expansion .
blocks.zh:
本节检验了统一法的中心范围主张. 我们问两个
问. 第一,能够表达计算机愿景的既定任务

删除, 由 WPM 评估的多少任务定义真实的新视觉
问题? 第一项问题措施是统一的;第二项措施是扩大的。

blocks.en:
We use Papers with Code as the historical reference because it maintained one
of the broadest public catalogs of computer-vision research, connecting named
tasks with papers, datasets, code, and benchmarks. Its final public records
contain 1,477 visual or vision-related tasks, which we use as a representative
inventory of the established field [ 65 ] . For
unification, we examine whether each historical task can be written as a route
through the WSM interfaces. For expansion, we compare the 1,148 tasks evaluated
by WSM v1 with this inventory and count the evaluated tasks that have no
historical counterpart. The complete matching rules and task-level records are
detailed in an expanded version.

blocks.en:
The result is direct. All 1,477 historical visual tasks can be expressed within
the WSM interfaces, giving 100% compatibility with the representative
historical inventory. After historical overlaps are removed, 655–1,056 of the
1,148 evaluated WSM tasks are new. Relative to the 1,477 established visual
tasks, WSM therefore expands the computer-vision task space by 44.3–71.5%.

Together, these findings establish both parts of the claim. WSM provides one
generative interface system for the established field of computer vision, and
it substantially enlarges that field with executable task definitions and
trained baselines. Its dense graph already contains 3,042 mappings, and
each newly aligned modality creates further families of estimation, generation,

existing task space and systematically creates new tasks beyond it.

blocks.en:
Position and interpretation of evidence. WSM makes three complementary claims, each supported at its appropriate
experimental scale. First, WSG and the four interfaces provide one operational
rule for expressing heterogeneous visual computations as directed generation.
Second, WSM v1 turns that rule into an executable system: 1,148 distinct
input–output tasks have their own trained TunnelingNets and end-to-end inference
results within one shared-backbone model.
Here, unified refers to the shared representation, generative backbone,
route-acquisition rule and router. Independently
optimized TunnelingNets remain sparsely activated components within that model, not
replications of the full backbone.

historical visual tasks, while the 1,148 figure separately measures tasks that
were actually trained and evaluated. Keeping these quantities distinct makes
the breadth claim directly auditable.

The validation scale was deliberately increased from tens of representative
routes, to hundreds of cross-family mappings, and finally to 1,148 frozen
tasks. Prior generalist vision systems commonly remain at tens of tasks, and
reports beyond one hundred are rare. WSM therefore moves the empirical frontier
to 1,148 separately trained and evaluated tasks: more than an order of
magnitude beyond even a 100-task system, 29 29 – 38 × 38\times beyond a
30–40-task system, and two to three orders beyond the conventional one-to-ten
task setting. These levels answer different questions: matched MTA–NJA ablations
isolate TunnelingNet acquisition behavior; QS/DAcc and 18,191 generated outputs
measure system-wide coverage; task-native metrics establish target-specific
quality; and AVIS, post-release imagery, and independent public annotations
establish transfer after acquisition. In this last setting, zero-shot and training-free mean that a route is trained once and then applied to
unseen datasets and annotation conventions without dataset-specific
retraining. Likewise, the reported budget ratios measure marginal task
acquisition after the respective pretrained priors, whereas the matched
attention ablations isolate the contribution of TunnelingNet itself. This
layered protocol evaluates scale without equating coverage with identical
ceiling accuracy: the complete score distributions and disclosed failure
regions identify which TunnelingNets merit further improvement while preserving the
system-level evidence that one method can acquire, register, and execute more
than one thousand visual tasks.

blocks.en:
Why a law, and why vision now? Empirical laws in artificial intelligence capture reproducible regularities over defined regimes. The canonical study Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models [ 66 ] examines cross-entropy under one autoregressive language-modeling
objective: the models are trained on WebText2, and the analysis establishes
predictive power laws over model size, dataset size, and compute, with trends
spanning six to eight orders of magnitude. Its importance does not come from
separately validating every NLP task, but from discovering a stable empirical
relation that compresses observations and predicts behavior outside individual
runs. In task diversity, that evidence centers on one learning objective; WSM
instead realizes one visual organizing principle through 1,148 separately trained
visual tasks, 39 output groups, four interfaces, and 18,191 generated outputs.
On a count of learning objectives,
one is less than 0.1% of 1,148. The two laws are validated along different scientific axes:
a scaling law is tested by depth along model, data, and compute scales, whereas
a unifying law is tested by breadth across heterogeneous visual tasks. The
breadth of 1,148 tasks directly supports the unification claim. The broader
scientific precedent is clear: an empirical law in AI is established by a
reproducible regularity over a defined regime.

blocks.en:
Computer vision is ready for an organizing law of its own. After decades of
progress measured mainly as separate models and benchmarks, the field needs a
principle that explains how those tasks relate and predicts how new ones can be
constructed. Scaling laws describe how performance changes as resources grow;
the Unified Law addresses what can be scaled—the modular visual capability space itself. The four interfaces make a concrete and refutable prediction: once task-relevant information is encoded as World Snapshots, heterogeneous visual computations and newly aligned visual information can be incorporated into the same generative formulation. WSM v1 provides the first thousand-task realization and unusually broad evidence for this principle. More broadly, WSM and LLMs can serve as peer foundations. An LLM unifies language and abstract reasoning; WSM unifies perception, generation, reconstruction, and control over explicit visual world states. Coupling these foundations could lead toward a general-purpose multimodal foundation model for universal task execution, in which linguistic intelligence and visual world intelligence operate as coequal, mutually conditioning capabilities. By these criteria, the Unified Law is a testable law-scale hypothesis supported by the first thousand-task realization. It opens a path from task-specific models toward general-purpose visual world intelligence.

blocks.en:
We presented the Unified Law for Visual Tasks, which expresses visual tasks as
transformations among image-like World Snapshots. World Snapshot Graphics
encodes RGB and auxiliary attributes in a representation with up to 256 channels, while
four interfaces express generation, estimation, conditional control, and
reconstruction in one generative formulation. Together, these interfaces and
TunnelingNet realize 1,148 evaluated visual tasks within a dense graph of 3,042
configured mappings. We validate both the method and the Unified Law at this scale, establishing
their effectiveness across more than one thousand tasks.

Our experiments show that TunnelingNet preserves the pretrained RGB-synthesis
prior while efficiently acquiring structured visual transformations, reaching
up to approximately 100 × 100\times greater training efficiency than the
parameter-matched native-attention baseline. Across all evaluated tasks,
WSM also achieves consistently strong performance, surpassing specialized prior
methods—including Best Paper and Best Paper Candidate systems—on the
reported metrics. The mathematical scalability of
the Unified Law further connects model growth to task growth: aligned
modalities expand direct-task breadth quadratically, visual chains expand
compositional depth exponentially, and independent task routes can be trained
in parallel. These routes are registered parameters of one modular WSM and are
sparsely activated by an explicit task key; independent optimization and
physical sharding do not make them standalone models. WSM therefore provides one extensible generative foundation for a
large and continually growing vocabulary of visual tasks. Its longer-term
trajectory is to unify, expand, and ultimately transcend the fixed task
boundaries of conventional Computer Vision.
